title: Data and analytics

noc.title: Data scientists
noc.applies_when: Statistical modelling, machine learning, predictive analysis. Only where the posting genuinely asks for modelling rather than reporting.

noc.applies_when: Requirements, process and systems analysis. Many business systems analyst and analytics analyst postings land here.

noc.title: Statistical officers and related research support

positioning:
Lead with the combination, because the combination is the unusual part: he can pull data through an API, clean and transform it in Python, query it in SQL, model it in Power BI, and then explain what it means to a client who does not care about any of that. Most junior analyst candidates have the middle three and not the ends. The pipeline work and the client reporting are what make the story coherent rather than a list of tools.

One thing to be ready for. These statuses are self-assessed rather than employer-verified, which is entirely normal for someone entering a lane, and it ships Tier A rows without any problem. What it does not do is survive a live SQL exercise on its own, and junior analyst screens are practical far more often than they are conversational. A public repo with a cleaned dataset, a documented SQL query set and a Power BI or matplotlib output turns the self-assessment into something an employer can check, and it is the single highest-leverage thing available in this lane. Note in the fit report whenever a posting asks for a portfolio or sets a take-home.
interview_watch: Expect a live or take-home SQL exercise. Window functions and CTEs are the two things most often tested beyond basics. Expect "tell me about a time the data said something the business did not want to hear", which rewards a real example from client reporting. Expect a case question: here is a metric that dropped, how would you find out why. Answer it as a structured decomposition, not a guess list.
pr_note: 21223, 21211, 21221 and 21222 are all TEER 1, among the strongest codes in the whole search. 12113 is TEER 2 and clears the floor. No RCIP community list covers any lane 5 NOC, so never tag a lane 5 role RCIP. AIP covers the lane entirely from a designated Atlantic employer, and Ontario's Workforce Priority stream takes any of them with a qualifying offer.
not_required: Machine learning beyond a basic conceptual understanding. Normal junior analyst roles do not ask for it, and a posting that hard-requires ML modelling is a 21211 data scientist seat that should be dropped rather than stretched into.

Status updated 2026-09-14. Keerthi reviewed the full matrix and confirmed he can do every Must-tier and Important-tier item. Statuses below are held on his own confirmation. Optional and Later items stay not yet by his own ordering.

notes.heading: What this changes for sourcing
notes.text: With the Must tier held, most junior analyst postings now grade Tier A rather than Tier C. The standard hard-required trio of SQL, Excel and Power BI is covered, so the lane should start producing volume rather than dropping nearly everything. Expect lane 5 to become one of the largest contributors to a Stream A run.
